object.content:
I did a #teardown of my Aunt's computer last night. I believe it's a Toshiba Satellite A205. The model number rubbed off from heavy use as it is a Windows Vista-era computer. It would not turn on at all and I checked all of the obvious things and I couldn't find anything wrong with it. I made this .pdf so I could keep track of the screws for reassembly. I'm sharing it because it may be helpful to someone else.
I wrote it using the Notes Plus app for iPad. It worked well but every time I switched to the camera to take photos, the app crashed. This app definitely takes a lot of memory and I don't think my original iPad mini can handle it.

object.content: The Toshiba does not turn on at all - no BIOS message, no Beeps? Did you disassemble the fan assembly and clean it - it's most likely clogged up with dust. Also, if you're not getting any display, most likely the GPU need's to be "re-balled". Over time, as the GPU keeps getting hot, the BGA solder ball contacts loosen and become dry joints. The solution is to take a  flame torch or hot air blower and heat the GPU to about 230 deg Celsius. I just did this for my brothers Dell and solved it. And I did the same hack for another Dell a few months ago. Here's a video : http://youtu.be/g1Ww5N1qF2M
I did blow out any dust I found but the computer was surprisingly clean. I can try your GPU trick. I have nothing to lose.
